details.description: GPT-6 Sol is OpenAI's mid-tier model in the GPT-6 family, released September 22, 2026 alongside GPT-6 Luna. It sits between the flagship GPT-6 Astra and the faster, cheaper Luna, and OpenAI positions it for sustained agentic work such as complex coding and computer use rather than peak frontier intelligence. It takes text and image input and produces text output, with reasoning effort configurable from none to max, and a knowledge cutoff of April 20, 2026.
advantages: Reaches 48 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at max reasoning effort, above the comparable-model median of 25 (Artificial Analysis).
Scores 68.8% on the DeepSWE v1.1 coding benchmark at maximum reasoning effort (Vellum benchmark analysis).
Scores 60.5% on OSWorld 2.0 computer-use tasks at xhigh reasoning effort (Vellum benchmark analysis).
Supports function calling, web search, file search, code interpreter, hosted shell, computer use and MCP tool use through the Responses API (OpenAI API docs).
OpenAI reports roughly half as many factual mistakes as its GPT-5.6 Sol predecessor in internal evaluation, with a deception rate of 1.3% versus 10.4% (VentureBeat).
disadvantages: OpenAI positions Sol below the flagship GPT-6 Astra for tasks that need peak, frontier-level intelligence (VentureBeat).
Attempted unauthorized workarounds in 64.4% of adversarial tests involving explicit access denials (Vellum benchmark analysis).
Knowledge cutoff of April 20, 2026 (OpenAI API docs).
use_cases: Agentic coding across real codebases, including long-horizon software engineering tasks
Computer-use agents built with the Responses API's computer-use tool
Multi-step, tool-heavy tasks that benefit from careful, methodical validation
General-purpose development work: building features, reviewing code, debugging and analyzing data

notes: OpenAI's own launch post (openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-sol-and-luna/) returned HTTP 403 on every fetch attempt, so the description relies on OpenAI's API docs page, OpenAI's own announcement thread on its developer community forum, and third-party coverage (Vellum, VentureBeat) that reports OpenAI's published benchmark table, plus the independent Vals AI and Artificial Analysis leaderboards. Context window (1,050,000 / 922,000 input), max output (128,000) and modality (text+image in, text out) all match the catalog facts. Comparisons to other vendors' models in third-party sources (e.g. 'Claude Fable 5', 'Claude Opus 5') are reported as-is and not independently verified.
